Both pass locally at -count=20, so it only shows under CI's timing.

THE ROOT CAUSE (confirmed, not a guess)
`closedServerURL()` at internal/remotehelper/transport/proxy_test.go:869:

    func closedServerURL() string {
        s := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(http.ResponseWriter, *http.Request) {}))
        url := s.URL
        s.Close()
        return url
    }

It manufactures a "guaranteed dead" node URL by starting a server and closing
it. Closing returns the port to the OS. Every test in that file is
t.Parallel(), so while one test is still using that URL as a dead node,
another test's httptest.NewServer can be handed the SAME port by the OS.

That is one event producing both failures:
- TestColdPathRedirectAllReplicasFail (path "/et/alice/repo") expects both dead
  replicas to fail so the proxy reports "all 2 nodes failed". One "dead" node
  was alive and answered 200, so require.Error got nil.
- TestServiceRPC owned the server that inherited the port, so the other test's
  request landed in its handler — which is exactly why it logged the foreign
  path /et/alice/repo/info/refs and method GET.

Neither test is wrong on its own. The helper hands out an address it does not
own. 12 call sites use it in that file, so this will keep firing.

THE FIX
Own the port for the test's lifetime instead of releasing it. Replace the
helper with one that keeps a listener bound and fails every connection:

    func deadServerURL(t *testing.T) string {
        t.Helper()
        l, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")
        require.NoError(t, err)
        t.Cleanup(func() { _ = l.Close() })
        go func() {
            for {
                c, err := l.Accept()
                if err != nil {
                    return
                }
                _ = c.Close() // dial connects, request never completes
            }
        }()
        return "http://" + l.Addr().String()
    }

Nothing else can bind the port because it stays held. Requests still fail, so
the existing assertions hold: "all 2 nodes failed" and "after entry-domain
redirect" come from the proxy's own aggregation, not from the dial error text.
It now needs a *testing.T, so update all 12 call sites to pass t.

Simpler alternative if you prefer a one-liner: return "http://127.0.0.1:0".
Connecting to port 0 fails immediately and nothing can ever bind it. Race-free,
but less faithful to "a node that went away" — your call which reads better.

VERIFY
- go test ./internal/remotehelper/transport/ -count=20   (and -race)
- Ideally -race with high -parallel to reproduce the interleaving; the bug is
  timing-dependent so a green run is necessary, not sufficient. The structural
  argument (the port is now owned) is the real proof.
- mise run fmt && mise run lint && mise run test:ci before pushing (repo
  requires it; lint after fmt, since fmt rewrites files).

STILL OPEN, NOT DIAGNOSED — separate issue, do not assume it is the same bug
A different flake was reported earlier on the same CI job:

Both flakes fixed. I stopped short of committing since you didn't ask.

## Flake 1 — `internal/remotehelper/transport` (the handoff's diagnosis)

I checked the diagnosis rather than taking it as given, and it holds. The decisive evidence is in the failure output itself: `TestServiceRPC` expects `/et/owner/repo/git-upload-pack` (proxy_test.go:224) but logged `path = /et/alice/repo/info/refs`. Requests can't cross between two httptest servers unless they shared a port, so two tests were using the same address at once.

Applied the suggested fix — `deadServerURL(t)` holds a listener bound for the test's lifetime and closes each connection it accepts, so nothing can take the port. Nothing in the package classifies dial errors or asserts on "connection refused", so trading refused-connection for reset-connection changes no assertion.

**Two more call sites the handoff missed.** `TestFailover` (:313) and `TestOnNodeFailedCalledOnConnectionError` (:364) hand-rolled the same close-and-keep-the-URL pattern inline, so they weren't in the 12-site grep. Left alone they'd keep firing the same flake while the fix looked complete. Both now use the helper.

Two deviations from your sketch, both forced by `mise run lint`: `noctx` rejects `net.Listen`, so it's `(*net.ListenConfig).Listen(t.Context(), …)`.

## Flake 2 — `internal/coreapi` (was undiagnosed)

Root cause found, and it's unrelated to the first one — you were right to retract the shared-cause guess.

`transportFor()` wrapped the process-global `http.DefaultTransport`. `httptest.Server.Close()` calls `http.DefaultTransport.CloseIdleConnections()` deliberately, as a courtesy to its users — stdlib source, `net/http/httptest/server.go:265-270`. Every parallel test in that package closes an httptest server, so each teardown wipes the pool that `TestRoundTripper_TokenCacheReusesExchanged` relies on between its two requests. It surfaces instead of retrying because `shouldRetryRequest` (`transport.go:842-861`) lists `errServerClosedIdle` but not `errCloseIdleConns`.

The chain is closed: `errCloseIdleConns` has exactly one producer in the whole stdlib (`transport.go:907`, inside `CloseIdleConnections`), and no code in this repo calls that on `DefaultTransport`. So `httptest.Server.Close` is the only reachable caller. `transportFor(t)` now clones `DefaultTransport` — same timeouts and proxy settings, private pool — which puts the error out of reach.

## On verification

Tests pass at `-count=20 -race` for both packages, and full `mise run test:ci` is green (unit + integration + canary, no FAIL lines).

I could not reproduce either flake locally, and I want to be straight about that rather than call them confirmed by test. macOS cycles through the whole ephemeral port range before wrapping, so flake 1's port reuse effectively can't happen here — 3000 interleaved open/close rounds gave zero collisions. For flake 2 I temporarily reverted my fix and ran a churn test alongside 13,692 keep-alive requests; still no failure, because the window between checking a connection out of the pool and writing to it is very narrow. Both reproductions were scratch-only and are deleted. The proof is structural — for flake 1 the cross-test request in the CI log, for flake 2 the single-producer argument above.

One unrelated thing: running the build tooling regenerated `.opencode/package-lock.json` with a batch of dependency bumps. I reverted it, since you didn't ask for a dependency change. Worth knowing it happens on any `mise run lint`/`test:ci`.

Two intermittent `test-core` failures. They surfaced together and look related, but the causes are separate. Both are test-only bugs — no production code changes.

## `internal/remotehelper/transport`

`closedServerURL()` built a "guaranteed dead" node by starting an `httptest.Server` and closing it. Closing hands the port back to the OS, and every test in that file runs with `t.Parallel()`, so another test's `httptest.NewServer` could be handed the same port while the first test still treated it as dead.

One event failed two tests at once:

- `TestColdPathRedirectAllReplicasFail` expects both replicas to fail. One "dead" node was alive and answered 200, so `require.Error` got nil.
- `TestServiceRPC` owned the server that inherited the port, so the other test's request landed in its handler — which is why it logged the foreign path `/et/alice/repo/info/refs` and method GET.

Neither test is wrong on its own. The helper handed out an address it did not own.

`deadServerURL(t)` replaces it: it keeps a listener bound for the test's lifetime and closes every connection it accepts. Nothing else can take the port, and requests still fail, so the existing assertions hold — "all 2 nodes failed" and "after entry-domain redirect" come from the proxy's own aggregation, not from the dial error text.

`TestFailover` and `TestOnNodeFailedCalledOnConnectionError` hand-rolled the same close-and-keep-the-URL pattern inline, so they were not among the 12 helper call sites. Left alone they would have kept firing the same flake. They use the helper now too.

## `internal/coreapi`

Undiagnosed before this change, and unrelated to the above.

`transportFor()` wrapped the process-global `http.DefaultTransport`. `httptest.Server.Close()` calls `http.DefaultTransport.CloseIdleConnections()` deliberately, as a courtesy to its users (`net/http/httptest/server.go:265-270`). Every parallel test in the package closes an httptest server, so each teardown wiped the connection pool that `TestRoundTripper_TokenCacheReusesExchanged` relies on between its two requests.

It surfaces instead of being retried because `shouldRetryRequest` (`net/http/transport.go:842-861`) lists `errServerClosedIdle` but not `errCloseIdleConns` — so it reaches the caller as `net/http: HTTP/1.x transport connection broken: http: CloseIdleConnections called`.

`transportFor(t)` now clones `DefaultTransport`: same timeouts and proxy settings, private pool. That puts the error out of reach — `errCloseIdleConns` has exactly one producer in the whole stdlib (`transport.go:907`, inside `CloseIdleConnections`), and nothing in this repo calls that on a private transport.

## Verification, and its limits

- `-count=20 -race` green on both packages.
- Full `mise run test:ci` green (unit + integration + canary).

Neither flake reproduced locally, and that is worth stating plainly rather than calling them confirmed by test. macOS cycles through the whole ephemeral port range before wrapping, so the port reuse in the first bug effectively cannot happen here — 3000 interleaved open/close rounds gave zero collisions. For the second, the fix was temporarily reverted and a churn test run alongside 13,692 keep-alive requests; still no failure, because the window between checking a connection out of the pool and writing to it is very narrow. Both reproductions were scratch-only and were deleted.

The proof is structural. For the first bug, the cross-test request in the CI log is decisive: `TestServiceRPC` expects `/et/owner/repo/git-upload-pack` but logged `/et/alice/repo/info/refs`, and requests cannot cross between two httptest servers unless they shared a port. For the second, the single-producer argument above.

The failure was **not** caused by my change — it's the same bug a third time, in `internal/entireclient/clusterdiscovery`, a package neither commit had touched. Fixed and pushed as `c33be0eb5`.

## What failed

Two tests went red on one event, the same signature as before:

```
TestResolve_PreAudienceEntryNotUsedAsDiscoveryFallback
  "...advertises no trusted core URLs..." does not contain "unreachable"

TestResolveContextForAPI/ambiguous_eligible_contexts
  expected: "/.well-known/entire-api.json"
  actual  : "/.well-known/entire-cluster.json"
```

Five tests built a client pinned to an `httptest.Server`'s host:port, then closed the server so discovery would fail (`resolve_test.go:276-278` and four siblings). Closing returns the port to the OS, another parallel test's `httptest.NewServer` gets handed it, and then the "unreachable" cluster answers — while that request lands in the *other* test's handler, where `apiHandler`'s in-handler path assertion reports the foreign cluster path.

That second assertion is what makes this conclusive rather than inferred: a cluster-discovery request cannot reach an api-discovery test's server unless the two shared a port.

## Fix

`deadPinningClient(t)` holds a listener for the test's lifetime and closes each connection it accepts. Requests still fail, and `fetchWellKnownJSON` wraps *any* transport error as `ErrUnreachable` (discovery.go:101-105) — I checked that before switching from connection-refused to connection-reset, since it's what keeps the `ErrUnreachable`/`ErrDiscoveryUnavailable` assertions valid.

I also gave these tests a private connection pool. That part is preventive rather than diagnosed here — this package shared `http.DefaultTransport` across parallel tests exactly the way `internal/coreapi` did in the first commit, and the same `httptest.Server.Close` teardown is all over it. Flagging it as a judgment call rather than a fix for an observed failure.

The other red job, `test / Check dependencies`, is just the gate that fails when `test-core` does — nothing separate to chase.

Both new helpers spawn an accept loop that returns on any Accept error while leaving the listener bound. If Accept fails for a reason other than the test cleanup closing it, the port stays bound with nobody accepting: later connects still complete via the kernel backlog, are never closed, and the request hangs instead of failing.

Go retries EINTR, ECONNABORTED and EAGAIN internally, so the realistic escape is fd exhaustion — not impossible in a heavily parallel suite that now holds an extra listener per dead node.

The failure mode is what makes this worth a line of insurance rather than a shrug. TestFailover and TestOnNodeFailedCalledOnConnectionError pass &http.Client{} with context.Background() — no timeout anywhere — so a hang becomes a package-level test timeout, which is exactly the kind of opaque CI failure this PR is trying to eliminate. input.content:
Three intermittent `test-core` failures across three packages. They share a shape — a test helper handing out state it does not own — but the causes are distinct. All test-only; no production code changes.

## 1. `internal/remotehelper/transport` — a port we gave back

`closedServerURL()` built a "guaranteed dead" node by starting an `httptest.Server` and closing it. Closing hands the port back to the OS, and tests in that file run with `t.Parallel()`, so another test's `httptest.NewServer` could be handed the same port while the first test still treated it as dead.

One event failed two tests at once:

- `TestColdPathRedirectAllReplicasFail` expects both replicas to fail. One "dead" node was alive and answered 200, so `require.Error` got nil.
- `TestServiceRPC` owned the server that inherited the port, so the other test's request landed in its handler — which is why it logged the foreign path `/et/alice/repo/info/refs` and method GET.

Neither test is wrong on its own. The helper handed out an address it did not own.

`deadServerURL(t)` replaces it: it keeps a listener bound for the test's lifetime and closes every connection it accepts. Nothing else can take the port, and requests still fail, so the existing assertions hold — "all 2 nodes failed" and "after entry-domain redirect" come from the proxy's own aggregation, not from the dial error text.

`TestFailover` and `TestOnNodeFailedCalledOnConnectionError` hand-rolled the same close-and-keep-the-URL pattern inline, so they were not among the 12 helper call sites. Left alone they would have kept firing the same flake. They use the helper now too.

## 2. `internal/coreapi` — a connection pool we shared

Undiagnosed before this change, and unrelated to the above.

`transportFor()` wrapped the process-global `http.DefaultTransport`. `httptest.Server.Close()` calls `http.DefaultTransport.CloseIdleConnections()` deliberately, as a courtesy to its users (`net/http/httptest/server.go:265-270`). Every parallel test in the package closes an httptest server, so each teardown wiped the connection pool that `TestRoundTripper_TokenCacheReusesExchanged` relies on between its two requests.

It surfaces instead of being retried because `shouldRetryRequest` (`net/http/transport.go:842-861`) lists `errServerClosedIdle` but not `errCloseIdleConns` — so it reaches the caller as `net/http: HTTP/1.x transport connection broken: http: CloseIdleConnections called`.

`transportFor(t)` now clones `DefaultTransport`: same timeouts and proxy settings, private pool. That puts the error out of reach — `errCloseIdleConns` has exactly one producer in the whole stdlib (`transport.go:907`, inside `CloseIdleConnections`), and nothing in this repo calls that on a private transport.

## 3. `internal/entireclient/clusterdiscovery` — the same port bug, third package

Found by CI on this very PR ([run 31710801422](https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/31710801422)), in a package neither earlier commit touched. Two tests, one event:

```
TestResolve_PreAudienceEntryNotUsedAsDiscoveryFallback
  "...advertises no trusted core URLs..." does not contain "unreachable"

TestResolveContextForAPI/ambiguous_eligible_contexts
  expected: "/.well-known/entire-api.json"
  actual  : "/.well-known/entire-cluster.json"
```

Five tests built a client pinned to an `httptest.Server`'s host:port and then closed the server so discovery would fail. The released port got picked up elsewhere, so the "unreachable" cluster answered — and the request landed in an api-discovery test's handler, where `apiHandler`'s in-handler path assertion reported the foreign cluster path.

That second assertion is what makes the diagnosis conclusive rather than inferred: a cluster-discovery request cannot reach an api-discovery test's server unless the two shared a port.

`deadPinningClient(t)` holds a listener for the test's lifetime and closes each connection it accepts. `fetchWellKnownJSON` wraps *any* transport error as `ErrUnreachable` (`discovery.go:101-105`), so the `ErrUnreachable` / `ErrDiscoveryUnavailable` assertions are unaffected by moving from connection-refused to connection-reset.

This package also shared `http.DefaultTransport` the way `coreapi` did, so it got the same private-pool treatment via `newTestTransport`. **That part is preventive, not diagnosed here.**

## Review findings addressed

- **The accept loops could hang instead of failing.** Both helpers returned from the accept goroutine on any `Accept` error while leaving the listener bound; a bound port with nobody accepting still completes the handshake from the kernel backlog, so a request would hang rather than fail — and these callers pass `context.Background()` with no client timeout, turning that into a package-level test timeout. Both loops now close the listener on the way out. Fd exhaustion is the realistic way in, since Go retries `EINTR`, `ECONNABORTED` and `EAGAIN` internally.
- **Two comments left wrong by the helper swap.** `deadServerURL` claimed "every test in this file runs with `t.Parallel()`" — 7 of 55 top-level tests do not, three of them `deadServerURL` callers. Go never overlaps a non-parallel top-level test with a parallel one, so those three were never exposed to the steal. The comment now names the pair that actually collided. Separately, "in-cluster (127.0.0.1) but unreachable" described the old helper, which failed at dial; the address is now reachable and simply never answers.
- **Duplication across packages, deliberately not extracted.** Two pairs of near-identical helpers now exist. Extracting them would mean standing up a new `internal/testutil` (the existing ones live under `cmd/entire/cli/` and `e2e/`), and the two listener helpers differ in return type. Recorded so a third copy triggers extraction instead of another paste.

## Verification, and its limits

- `-count=20 -race -parallel 16` green on all three packages.
- Full `mise run test:ci` green (unit + integration + canary).

None of these reproduced locally, and that is worth stating plainly rather than calling them confirmed by test. macOS cycles through the whole ephemeral port range before wrapping, so the port reuse effectively cannot happen here — 3000 interleaved open/close rounds gave zero collisions. For the pool bug, the fix was temporarily reverted and a churn test run alongside 13,692 keep-alive requests; still no failure, because the window between checking a connection out of the pool and writing to it is very narrow. Both reproductions were scratch-only and deleted.

The proof is structural rather than empirical:

- For the port bugs, the cross-test requests in the CI logs are decisive — `TestServiceRPC` expects `/et/owner/repo/git-upload-pack` but logged `/et/alice/repo/info/refs`, and `apiHandler` expects `/.well-known/entire-api.json` but logged `/.well-known/entire-cluster.json`. Requests cannot cross between two httptest servers unless they shared a port.
- For the pool bug, `errCloseIdleConns` has exactly one producer in the stdlib, and `httptest.Server.Close` is the only caller reachable from these tests.

## Worth a follow-up

Three packages have now hit the same bug, and the repo-wide sweep only happened after CI failed rather than when the first fix went in. A lint rule, or a shared "address that never answers" helper, would be worth more than three point fixes — otherwise the fourth instance gets written next month. Deliberately out of scope here.
